title: Certified Optimal Measurement Reduction over Quantum Context Landscapes
abstract: Quantum-measurement reduction contains two distinct global-optimization layers: a continuous problem of splitting an observable and allocating shots within a fixed measurement dictionary, and a nonconvex outer problem of designing the dictionary and calibrating its data-driven uncertainty model. We solve the inner layer globally and certifiably as a second-order cone program (SOCP), and use RANGE, a robust adaptive nature-inspired global optimizer, for the combinatorial and statistical outer layer. For any declared set of contexts, per-shot costs, score functions, and covariance model, the SOCP returns the minimum leading shot cost among unbiased linear stratified estimators. The conic dual supplies an independently checkable lower-bound witness; after feasibility repair, an external verifier recomputes $L \le Φ\le U$ from stored data without trusting the optimizer. Pilot measurements yield simultaneous finite-sample covariance brackets, and the dual becomes a pricing oracle for omitted contexts. Discrete RANGE searches covering sub-dictionaries, Pareto compression fronts, and candidate contexts; continuous RANGE performs an explicitly empirical, coverage-constrained calibration of covariance-radius models, while rigorous certificates retain the proved finite-sample radius. RANGE compresses molecular context dictionaries by 4.3-6.1x at 0.2-2.1% certified-frontier excess. Standard strategies are exactly optimal for H2 yet leave factors of 2.1-7.7 in shots within their own settings by H2O. Adding fully commuting contexts lowers the certified optimum by up to 56%; on 29-35-qubit production f-element Hamiltonians under a declared Hartree-Fock-proxy covariance model, the capped-dictionary enlargement saves 31-70% of the shots, and transformations reducing block-encoding cost need not reduce sampling cost.
summary: This paper presents a comprehensive theoretical framework for optimizing quantum measurement reduction by estimating observable expectation values. It tackles the problem using a combination of Second-Order Cone Programming (SOCP) for continuous allocation and advanced global optimization techniques for dictionary design. The key contribution is providing mathematically certified lower bounds on the required shot count, making resource estimation rigorous and verifiable.
main_problem: The core problem is optimizing quantum measurement reduction, which requires solving two coupled global optimization layers: an inner continuous shot allocation problem and an outer nonconvex dictionary design problem.
main_result: The authors develop a framework that solves the inner layer certifiably using Second-Order Cone Programming (SOCP) and uses a robust optimizer (RANGE) for the outer layer, achieving significant compression of measurement dictionaries while maintaining certified optimality bounds.
method: The methodology combines convex optimization (SOCP) for shot allocation with adaptive global optimization (RANGE) for dictionary design. Crucially, it establishes verifiable lower-bound certificates via the conic dual and incorporates robust analysis using covariance sandwiching for finite-sample guarantees.
model_or_system: The theory applies to estimating expectation values $\langle H angle$ of observables $H$ in quantum systems. The measurement process is modeled by defining a dictionary of available contexts, each associated with a visible subspace and an estimated covariance model.
key_observables: Minimum leading shot cost ($\Phi$), expected value $\langle H angle$, certified lower/upper bounds ($L, U$), and the required number of shots ($N_\ell$).
important_parameters: Shot costs ($c_\ell$), measurement context definitions ($	ext{V}_\ell$), covariance matrices ($\Gamma_\ell$), and confidence parameters ($\delta$ for finite-sample bounds).
main_assumptions: The framework assumes the existence of a measurable dictionary of contexts. Robustness theorems address uncertainty in estimating the covariance matrices from pilot data.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates measurement reduction as a combination of geometric constraints (visible subspaces) and optimization, with the dual providing a certificate bounding all possible schedules.
paper_structure: The paper builds by first defining the two-layer optimization problem. It then solves the inner layer via SOCP, establishing the primal/dual relationship. Subsequent sections introduce robust analysis for finite samples using covariance bounds (Theorem 3 & 4), culminating in a certified repair procedure to ensure mathematical validity.
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous, mathematically verifiable tools to determine the minimum required experimental resources (shots) needed to estimate quantum observables, moving beyond heuristic optimization methods common in quantum simulation and characterization.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Measurement reduction as geometry plus optimization. The allowed contexts define visible subspaces. A covariance model, obtained from a proxy state or from pilot data, turns each visible subspace into a variance norm. The optimal decomposition and shot allocation are obtained by a conic program. The dual returns a certificate that lower-bounds every schedule in the declared landscape and, through column generation, identifies whether useful contexts are missing.
